transcript.dialogue: I'm Mira. Careful with that handshake, or you'll get blue ink all over your cuffs. Did you just come straight from a studio?
I'm Dex. Yeah, just working with clay today—though trust me, the ink is cleaner than what I usually bring home.
Clay is honest work, at least. Does it take over your whole kitchen or do you manage to keep it in the studio?
It stays in the studio mostly. Though my kitchen table has a permanent grey dusting I've stopped fighting.
My apartment smells like old paper and tea, but my kitchen table is strictly off-limits for drafting. I only draw where the Tuesday trams run.
transcript.action: traces a circle on the napkin

transcript.dialogue: I used to do fire stunts, actually. Nineteen times on the payroll. Mostly I just miss the warmth, though I don't miss the smell of the gel.
Nineteen times? You're lucky you still have eyebrows. Though honestly, my imaginary transit lines are way safer than setting yourself on fire.
Yeah, the eyebrows are mostly survivors. Honestly, walking out into this quiet air feels pretty good.
It really does. Have a good walk home, Dex—let me know if you ever need a map for the studio.
Thanks, Mira. Honestly, walking beside someone who doesn't mind a quiet street is the best map I could ask for tonight.
